name: Crime & Punishment
caption: The PWA's own Tag Team Champions, who beat Devastation for the unified FWF/PWA titles at the Clash of the Masters on a fall taken with a foot on the bottom rope.
notes: The FWF's own tag ledger names Punisher Lang of the two; the other half is not recovered. the WeWF's own "TWIW - Summer Recap of E-Wrestling - Pt.I" (27 September 1992), structured under the anti-double-count rule (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-summer-recap-of-e-wrestling-pt-i-1992-09-27.html) records a loss to the L.A. Looters, engineered by the Looters' own manager Nate X injecting a syringe into a Crime & Punishment wrestler billed only as "Jailhouse Rock" — too ambiguous a mention (the text doesn't settle whose man he was) to attach as this unit's own second member.

caption: Primetime Pete and Bang-bang Bobby, who wrestled as the Rock and Roll Maniacs until a lost Name Match against their own former partners RnR left them, by the recap's own account, simply "the Maniacs."

identity.note: WeWF's own "the-maniacs-wewf" (turn 6, January 1991, members billed only "Maniac #1"/"Maniac #2") carries the exact same name, but this PWA team's own name is earned IN this recap's own text (losing a Name Match while billed "the Rock and Roll Maniacs"), a full year after WeWF's own team already carried the name — an origin story that contradicts rather than supports a migration, and neither member's name matches the WeWF row's anonymous pair. Filed distinct under the no-auto-merge rule; a coincidental landing on a generic name, not the RnR/Lord Rod pattern beside it.

notes: A third figure billed only as "Elvis" accompanies this team ringside for one interference spot early in the recap and is never otherwise developed or named again — too thin a namedrop to mint as its own character row.
